Collecting the signing-failure details from the sessions that worked on the Mac runner.
Here is a brief you can paste into another agent. I built it from the release session's reports and checked the branch, commits and files against the repo. I haven't re-run any of the tests it describes.
Problem: the self-hosted Mac build runner builds JusPrin but can't sign it
JusPrin's release workflow can send its Mac jobs to a GitHub Actions runner on Kenneth's Mac instead of GitHub's hosted Macs. On that Mac, both chips build cleanly, but the last job fails. That job joins the Apple Silicon and Intel builds into one universal app, signs it and notarises it. Until signing works there, release builds can't use Kenneth's Mac.
Why the self-hosted Mac is wanted

* Capacity: GitHub's Apple Silicon Macs sometimes have no capacity. On 2026-11-19, GitHub cancelled one build partway through, after 942 of its 1,008 build steps, "due to capacity constraints".
* No Homebrew: GitHub's Mac images come with Homebrew, so the app's bundled Python links Homebrew's `liblzma`. It shipped that way in 2.0.0 and 2.0.1. A build on a Mac without Homebrew avoids this. Another session ("Mac app Python liblzma linking") is separately trying to fix this on GitHub's Macs by building xz itself.

Current setup on Kenneth's Mac

* The runner: it runs as a separate macOS user, `jusprin-ci`, from `/Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner`. It is installed as a LaunchDaemon, a background service that starts without anyone logging in.
* The setup script: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/setup-jusprin-ci-user.sh`. It needs `sudo`, so Kenneth runs it himself. Never type his password.
* The repository variable: `JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER` is deleted, so every release builds on GitHub's Macs for now. Setting it again sends the release's Mac jobs, including signing, to Kenneth's Mac. Only set it once signing works there and the fixes below are on `main`.

The fixes so far

* Where they are: the local branch `claude/self-hosted-mac-kept-deps` has eight commits, from 264be5defe to 297e0edccb. It is not pushed and is behind `jusprin-dev`, so it needs a rebase onto ed25d6d94a. The worktree is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/self-hosted-mac-kept-deps`.
* What they change:
   * They keep Homebrew, MacPorts and XQuartz libraries out of the built libraries and the app: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/mac_self_hosted.cmake`, and a check in `mac_outside_links.sh`.
   * They check the build tools before building.
   * They build on GitHub's Macs by default, with a box on the release form to use the self-hosted Mac instead.
   * They import Apple's Developer ID intermediate certificates into the signing keychain.
* The test branch: `claude/mac-runner-test` on GitHub. It falls back to the runner label `jusprin-release-mac` when the variable is empty.

What failed and why

* The error: `codesign` said "unable to build chain to self-signed root", then `errSecInternalComponent`. This happened in test runs on 2026-11-19.
* Ruled out: a missing Apple intermediate certificate. The second run imported both intermediates, each checked against a fixed SHA-256, and failed the same way.
* The leading explanation, still unproven: Apple's developer-support engineers say that signing from a LaunchDaemon that runs as a user is a "mixed execution context". It is unreliable, and they advise against it. They support signing only as a logged-in user, either at the login window or over SSH. GitHub's own installer, `svc.sh`, sets the runner up on macOS as a LaunchAgent, which runs only while its user is logged in. The sources:
   * https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/774832
   * https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/712005
   * https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/700760

Decision needed (Kenneth's)

1. A LaunchAgent in a logged-in `jusprin-ci` session (recommended): this is how GitHub's installer sets it up and matches Apple's guidance. Kenneth logs in as `jusprin-ci` once after each restart through fast user switching, then switches back to his own account. That session stays open in the background and uses some memory.
2. Build on Kenneth's Mac, sign on a GitHub Mac: nothing changes on his Mac. When GitHub has no Mac at all, the release still can't finish.
3. Sign over SSH to the same Mac: this needs Remote Login turned on, which is a security setting. Not recommended.

Also unresolved: security

* The risk: the repository is public, TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin. A self-hosted runner there could run code from a fork's pull request on Kenneth's Mac.
* What to confirm before landing: no workflow that runs on pull requests can reach the self-hosted runner label.

What done looks like

* Kenneth's pick is carried out.
* A test run signs and notarises the universal app on Kenneth's Mac.
* `spctl` and `stapler validate` pass on the disk image.
* Kenneth's own keychain list is the same afterwards as before.
* The branch is rebased and landed on `jusprin-dev` with Kenneth's yes.
* `JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER` is set again.

Rules:

* Don't push, set repository variables or change macOS settings without Kenneth's yes.
* Never type passwords.
* One build at a time on that Mac.

The session notes in `release-2.0.1-after-publish.md`, in the same folder as the setup script, have the full history.

#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.
#
# Run it from Kenneth's own account, in Terminal:
#
#   sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
#     bash "<this file>"
#
# It asks for Kenneth's password (sudo), then for a password for the new
# account (sysadminctl). Nobody needs to log in as that account afterwards.
# Running it again skips what is already done.
#
# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the seven
#    tools the build needs. Kenneth's /opt/homebrew is not touched.
# 3. Downloads the GitHub Actions runner into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner,
#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.
set -euo pipefail

ci_user=jusprin-ci
home=/Users/$ci_user
repo=TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
label=jusprin-release-mac
name=kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci
runner_version=2.338.2
runner_sha=25a065af409ffa317ab4d5a3b614dd15fc9c40f2172bc1b35a1b1258e919a388
tools="automake libtool texinfo pkgconf yasm nasm gettext"
path="$home/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
plist=/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist

if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  echo "Run this with sudo (see the top of the file)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${RUNNER_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "RUNNER_TOKEN is empty: run it as the top of the file shows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

as_ci() {
  sudo -u "$ci_user" env -i HOME="$home" USER="$ci_user" LOGNAME="$ci_user" LANG=en_US.UTF-8 \
    PATH="$path" HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1 "$@"
}

echo "== 1. The account"
if ! id "$ci_user" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Type a password for the new account $ci_user:"
  sysadminctl -addUser "$ci_user" -fullName "JusPrin CI" -shell /bin/zsh -home "$home" -password -
  dscl . create "/Users/$ci_user" IsHidden 1
fi
createhomedir -c -u "$ci_user" > /dev/null
id "$ci_user"

echo "== 2. Its own Homebrew and the build tools"
if [ ! -x "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  as_ci git clone -q --depth 1 https://github.com/Homebrew/brew "$home/homebrew"
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
as_ci "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" install $tools

echo "== 3. The runner"
runner=$home/actions-runner
as_ci mkdir -p "$runner" "$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner"
if [ ! -x "$runner/config.sh" ]; then
  tarball=$runner/runner.tar.gz
  as_ci curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
    "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v$runner_version/actions-runner-osx-arm64-$runner_version.tar.gz"
  echo "$runner_sha  $tarball" | shasum -a 256 -c -
  as_ci tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$runner"
  rm -f "$tarball"
fi
if [ ! -f "$runner/.runner" ]; then
  as_ci bash -c "cd '$runner' && ./config.sh --unattended --url 'https://github.com/$repo' \
    --token '$RUNNER_TOKEN' --name '$name' --labels '$label' --work _work"
fi
# Jobs get this PATH: never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
echo "$path" | as_ci tee "$runner/.path" > /dev/null
# The service starts runsvc.sh from the runner's folder, as the runner's own
# svc.sh install puts it there.
as_ci cp "$runner/bin/runsvc.sh" "$runner/runsvc.sh"
as_ci chmod u+x "$runner/runsvc.sh"

echo "== 4. The service"
new_plist=$(mktemp)
cat > "$new_plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.jusprin.ci-runner</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>$runner/runsvc.sh</string>
    </array>
    <key>UserName</key>
    <string>$ci_user</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>$runner</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
      <key>SuccessfulExit</key>
      <false/>
    </dict>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stderr.log</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
      <key>ACTIONS_RUNNER_SVC</key>
      <string>1</string>
      <key>HOME</key>
      <string>$home</string>
      <key>USER</key>
      <string>$ci_user</string>
      <key>LANG</key>
      <string>en_US.UTF-8</string>
      <key>PATH</key>
      <string>$path</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
    <key>SessionCreate</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
EOF
# Restarting the service ends the job it is running, so it is restarted only
# when the service file changed or the service is not loaded.
if cmp -s "$new_plist" "$plist" && launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  rm -f "$new_plist"
  echo "The service is unchanged and loaded; left running."
else
  mv "$new_plist" "$plist"
  chown root:wheel "$plist"
  chmod 644 "$plist"
  launchctl bootout system "$plist" 2> /dev/null || true
  launchctl bootstrap system "$plist"
  sleep 5
fi
launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner | grep -E "state|pid" | head -3
echo "Done. The runner $name should show as Idle on GitHub within a minute."

The search turned up many matching reports, but no single confirmed fix for this exact setup (self-hosted GitHub Actions runner as a LaunchDaemon on macOS).

**Likely causes**
- Apple DTS has explained the warning this way: the self-signed root cannot be found, there's a missing WWDR intermediate certificate, or Keychain Access is being used to customize the trust settings on either the intermediate or root certificate.
- A LaunchDaemon session often can't see the user's login keychain. One developer reported that SessionCreate=true with a local keychain failed with errSecInternalComponent, and SessionCreate=false failed with "The specified item could not be found in the keychain."

**Fixes people reported**
- Adding the WWDR intermediate to the System keychain. One answer on a LaunchDaemon runner case says WWDR Intermediates must be in the System.keychain? This is a community suggestion, not an Apple-confirmed fix.
- Checking trust settings. Apple's guidance is that if the chain fails, make sure that none of these certificates have customised trust settings.
- Unlocking the keychain in the job. In one GitHub Actions case, running a security unlock-keychain command beforehand made creating the .xcarchive pass.

**Caveat for newer macOS**
A developer on Sequoia reported that workarounds like placing the codesigning cert + private key in a custom keychain and unlocking it in the session of the LaunchDaemon don't work anymore. Common alternatives suggested are running the runner in a GUI login session, using screen sharing, or signing over SSH in that user's context (have the server auto login in as GUI user and start your job runner in that context.).

I'd check the System keychain for the WWDR intermediate first, then confirm trust settings in Keychain Access, and test whether the same command succeeds from a GUI session. If it does, the problem is the daemon's keychain session rather than the certificate.

One developer on Apple's forums describes this exact setup failing with `errSecInternalComponent`. Another says that on macOS Sequoia and later, a custom keychain unlocked inside a LaunchDaemon no longer works. This Mac runs macOS 26.3.
- **Other causes, ruled out:** this Mac has no admin-level certificate trust overrides. Your own login keychain holds three valid "Developer ID Application: TSD Technology" identities.
- **Still a hypothesis:** I couldn't run `codesign` inside the daemon's context to prove it, because that needs `sudo`. The test run after your pick will prove or disprove it.

**Security of the public repo**

- Forks' pull requests need a maintainer's approval before any workflow runs. This is set to "all external contributors", the strictest setting GitHub offers.
- Every workflow that runs on pull requests uses GitHub's Ubuntu machines; none can reach the self-hosted label.
- One risk remains. A fork's pull request can edit a workflow to target the `jusprin-release-mac` label, and it would run on your Mac once a maintainer approves it. TheSpaghettiDetective is on GitHub's Free plan, so I'd expect it can't limit the runner to particular workflows: that needs runner groups, a paid feature. I couldn't confirm this, because my GitHub token can't read the org's runner settings. Anyone approving a fork's PR should first check that it doesn't touch `.github/`.

**Decision needed:** how should the `jusprin-ci` runner run so that signing works?

- **Option 1, my pick:** the runner becomes a LaunchAgent, a service that runs only while `jusprin-ci` is logged in. This is how GitHub's own installer sets it up, and it matches Apple's guidance. The cost: after each restart you log in once as `jusprin-ci` through fast user switching, then switch back. That session stays open in the background and uses some memory. I'd update the setup script; you'd run it with `sudo` and log in once.
- **Option 2:** build on your Mac, but sign and notarise on a GitHub Mac. Nothing changes on your Mac. The cost: when GitHub has no Macs at all, the release still can't finish.
- **Option 3:** sign over SSH to this Mac. It needs Remote Login turned on, a security setting, so I don't recommend it.

Is Option 1 the one you want?
